about: The wire between the Keel daemon's phone API (/v1, src/integrations/mobile/v1.ts) and the phone app (android/), written once.

The daemon is checked against it by src/integrations/mobile/v1.test.ts (the wire contract), the app by android/app/src/test/java/dev/avifenesh/keel/ContractTest.kt. Neither needs a phone, a push service or a model.
signing: the bytes each side signs or verifies, from the same inputs.
fields: per shape, the fields the app reads, name to JSON type. A dot goes into an object. `?` marks a field the daemon may leave out; `|null` one that may be null.
examples: per shape, answers and frames as the daemon sends them (for send and answer: bodies as the app sends them).

Both directions are checked. The daemon sends every field of every shape under its name and type. The app has a reader for every field, and reads no field of the daemon's that no shape names: its JSON reading is in Wire.kt and Feed.kt only, and ContractTest reads those sources.
The daemon may add fields to any shape; the app ignores a field it does not know. Renaming or dropping a listed field, or changing the signed bytes, breaks one of the checks.

The shapes by route: sync (GET /v1/sync, and `sync` in the stream's hello), page (GET /v1/chats/:id/messages?paged=1), receipt (POST /v1/chats/:id/messages), created (POST /v1/chats), resolved (POST /v1/approvals/:id), pulse (GET /v1/pulse), usage (GET /v1/chats/:id/usage), me (GET /v1/me), push_config (GET /v1/push-config), paired (POST /v1/pair), revoked (DELETE /v1/devices/:id), errors (GET /v1/errors), error_marked (POST /v1/errors/:id/read, /unread or /resolve), error (the body of any refusal), push (the data of one push), and the frames of GET /v1/events by their type.

errors lists the daemon's open errors as the page's Errors panel does, the newest first: each kind of failure once with its whole message, `count` the times it happened, `first` and `last` in seconds, `read` out of the count, `recovered` healed by a retry, and the session it last happened in (`chat_id`, `title`) while that session is there; `sessions` says in how many it happened when more than one. `unread` is the page's badge: open, not read, not recovered. An `unwritten-` id is one the store could not take yet; read or resolved, it is let go, and it cannot be marked unread.
sync.more is false from this daemon; an app reads it for a daemon that pages its catch-up.

upload and upload_ref are the daemon's side of attaching a file: the answer to POST /v1/upload?name=<name>&mime=<type> with the file's bytes as the body (the example is the answer for a 1x1 PNG named photo.png), and how a prompt names it in `attachments`. The app uploads each file when it is picked and sends a prompt that names the uploads (send.attachments, each an upload_ref). It checks a file against me.uploads.max_bytes before it sends the bytes, and scales a photo to me.uploads.image_edge on its long edge (the edge the daemon stores a photo at). The stored message lists what it carried in meta.attachments, an image under a `media` id that GET /v1/media/<media> serves.

A permission card that waits carries what the read-first rule needs (src/safety/card.ts, the one form every client gets): `text` is the whole text to judge with each hidden character written as its code point, `notes` say why it is asked, where it runs, what in the text can mislead and whether only its start is here, `rtl` says it holds letters written right to left, and `hold` says why Allow needs the text shown whole first (long, cut, marked, risk, where). An empty `hold` means one line shows all of it. The app sends `seen: "whole"` with an allow once all of `text` was on its screen. An allow of a held card without `seen` is answered 409 with the sentence to show in `error`, and the card stays open: an app from before these fields shows that sentence. `grants` are the rules a standing answer would store: the session action's label names them, and the app's button does ("Allow echo * for this session"). The action is offered only where there is a rule. `line` is what a notification says of the request (the tool, where it runs when not here, the text), and `glance` says that a collapsed notification shows all of that line: only then may a notification carry Allow once. A push says the same: its `body` is that line, its `opts` hold `once` only for such a request, and `hold` gives the reasons a request is held (comma separated; empty when none). An answer given from a notification says `via: "notification"`: it never counts as having shown the text, it allows once only what `glance` covers, and it gives no standing answer (409 with the sentence). A closed card says where it was answered in `from`. An answer to a card that was already answered is a 409 whose `error` says how it ended, who answered and how long ago ("this approval is already allowed (once) from the page, 3 s ago"), with the closed card in `approval`.

A plan the model presents in plan mode is a card of kind `plan`: `command` is its title, `text` the whole plan, `hold` ["plan"] (approved only once all of it was on the screen, with `seen: "whole"` and the approval key). Its actions: `session` approves it with the work going on in auto edits, `once` in ask (each change asks; what a phone with no screen lock may start), `deny` sends it back to planning, with `feedback` in the answer when the owner wrote what to change. A closed plan card says `approved` with the choice it was approved with, or `denied`, or `expired` when the turn ended under it.

changes (GET /v1/chats/:id/changes) is what a session changed in its folder, read-only: `turns` newest first, each with its files (file_change: git's status letter, lines added and removed, `outside` for a write made outside the session's turns), and `session`, the files changed since its first turn. `n` is the turn's place among the session's turns, as the page numbers it; `turn` is what /changes/diff takes. file_diff (GET /v1/chats/:id/changes/diff?path=<path>[&turn=<turn>]) is one file's unified diff, of one turn or since the first; `truncated` says it was cut where the page cuts a diff. `unavailable` says why there is nothing to show (the session's files are on another machine, no checkpoints are kept).

A session an agent works in has its starter's id in `parent_id`; an agent's agents have that agent's session there, so the rows make the tree. `agents` counts the agents at work below a session, at any depth; `state_word` is the state in the workbench's own words; `created` orders an agent among its siblings. A live agent's row says what it is doing now, as its line on the workbench does (src/automation/now.ts): `now` is the newest sentence of its thinking or the call it runs, `now_steps` its model steps, `now_since` when its task began (seconds), `now_usd` what it spent, `now_need` 1 when it waits on the owner. The daemon sends a row again with a new line at most every 15 s an agent.

start (GET /v1/start) is what a new session can start with: the default `model` and the `models` to pick from, the `folders` this machine's sessions worked in (newest first, the daemon's own folder marked `home`), and the `machines` of the fleet that take a session (`ready` while it answers; `root`, the folder granted there). new_chat is the body of POST /v1/chats: each field may be left out (the default model, the daemon's folder, this machine); `workspace` is an absolute folder here, or one inside `root` on another machine; `text` is the first message, sent at once.

away (GET /v1/away) is the digest of the owner's last absence, the page's own, in words: `span` (when), `brief` (one line), `totals`, what the daemon went through (`daemon`), and the sessions in which something happened, the one that failed first, each with its facts and the part that went wrong (`bad`). Null when the owner was not away or nothing happened. DELETE /v1/away says it was seen: it is shown no more, here or on the page. POST /v1/presence with `idle_ms` says the owner touched the app that long ago: the phone in use ends an absence, as a page in use does.

A push of kind `withdraw` takes notifications down. With `aid`, the one request's: it was answered elsewhere while its session still has something unread, and `c` is empty, so an app from before takes nothing down for it. Without `aid`, everything shown for the session `c`: nothing in it is unread any more.

A push of kind `live` is the lasting notification's news: `w` sessions working, `q` cards waiting on the owner, `title` and `body` to show as they are, `since` (epoch milliseconds) when the longest turn started. The push service keeps only the newest (one collapse key). `w` and `q` of 0 take the notification down. The background check reads the same status from `live` in GET /v1/pulse, with the same fields.

A chat row carries `h`, eight hex digits of its content. A reconnecting phone says what it holds in a bounded number of bytes (`held` on GET /v1/events or /v1/sync): its rows go into `n` buckets by `fnv(id) % n`, and each bucket is said by eight hex digits, the sum mod 2^32 of `fnv("<id>:<h>")` over its rows (FNV-1a, 32 bits, over UTF-8; an empty bucket is 00000000), joined by dots in bucket order, `n` of them (at most 256). The catch-up then sends only the rows of the buckets whose digest differs, with `buckets` naming them (`n`, and `of`, their indices) and `complete` false: the phone drops each row it holds in those buckets that was not sent. `held` at the top of this file is a worked example. A whole read (since 0, or a cursor that cannot be caught up from), and a `held` not of this form, send every row.

search (GET /v1/search?q=<words>) is the page's search across sessions: titles first, then what was said and done, one hit a session at most. A hit's `snippet` holds the words found between  and ; `kind` says where (title, user, assistant, tool_use, tool_result, summary). `limits` says in words what the query limited the search to (state:failed, since:yesterday).

helper (GET /v1/helper, PATCH /v1/helper with `on`) is the owner's helper: whether it is on, its conversation (`chat_id`, a chat of the list marked `helper`), how many records its memory holds, and what it was told lately, newest first (helper_event: `chat_id` is the session it is about, null for mail). Turning it on makes its conversation the first time. memory (GET /v1/helper/memory[?q=<words>]) is its memory's records (memory_record), found by key, alias, topic or words with `q`; DELETE /v1/helper/memory/<key> forgets one. A daemon that runs no helper answers 409.

What waits on the owner is in the order of the next-look queue (src/core/wait-rank.ts): the costliest wait first, then the one asked first. A pending card says when its alert was first raised (`asked`, seconds) and what its wait costs: `wait` holds the facts it began with (`at` and `until` in seconds; `key`, what the wait costs a minute in dollars, is the order's key and never changes while the card waits), `wait_line` what it costs as it stands when the card is sent (the agents that wait then, the cache's life then), in words. The app orders the cards that wait by `wait.key`, then `asked` (a card without one, its `ts`), then `id`. A push of an ask whose wait costs something also carries the words as they stand in `cost` and the key in `wk` (the app does not read them yet).
